papers.title: DiCE-Ex: a web server for network-based differential-centrality gene exploration.
papers.summary: Web server DiCE-Ex builds condition-specific weighted PPI networks from expression data and flags genes whose network centrality shifts between conditions, catching rewired non-hub regulators that standard differential expression misses. Case studies recover known disease modulators and nominate candidates for mechanistic validation.

papers.title: Lactylation-mediated activation of HSPA5 upregulates VGLL3 expression to inhibit mitophagy-dependent ferroptosis following intracerebral hemorrhage.
papers.summary: In intracerebral hemorrhage models, a lactylation-driven HSPA5-VGLL3-EGLN3-HIF1α axis suppresses BNIP3/BNIP3L-mediated mitophagy-dependent ferroptosis. Pharmacologic HSPA5 activation (BIX) protected cultured neurons and improved motor function in mice, suggesting a therapeutic strategy against hemorrhagic neuronal injury.

papers.title: RABC1 regulates ER-phagy to maintain er homeostasis in plants.
papers.summary: The plant small GTPase RABC1 is recruited to ATG8E-positive autophagosomes upon ER stress and interacts with exocyst component SEC5A. RABC1 mutants show impaired autophagic flux and ER membrane turnover, supporting a model where RABC1 is a stress-responsive switch coupling ER stress signals to ER-phagy.

papers.title: Kamino: fast proteome-wide variant calling for amino acid phylogenomics.
papers.summary: Kamino is a reference- and alignment-free tool that builds amino-acid phylogenomic alignments directly from proteomes using recoded k-mer occupancy. It accurately recovers M. tuberculosis lineages, GTDB taxa, and drosophila/mammalian phylogenies, running orders of magnitude faster than marker-based pipelines; implemented in Rust.

papers.title: Protective role of probiotics or Spirulina platensis supplementation against mercury-induced hematological, histopathological, and antioxidant-immune gene dysregulation in Nile Tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus).
papers.journal: Biometals : an international journal on the role of metal ions in biology, biochemistry, and medicine
papers.summary: In Nile tilapia exposed to mercury, supplementation with probiotics (Bacillus/Lactobacillus spp.) or Spirulina platensis restored hematological parameters, reduced erythrocyte abnormalities and gill damage, and normalized antioxidant (SOD, CAT) and immune cytokine gene expression, supporting dietary mitigation of mercury toxicity in aquaculture.

papers.title: Genome wide transcriptional changes underlie gradual and recurrent adaptation to protein malnutrition in zebrafish.
papers.summary: Zebrafish pllp mutants, which normally die from protein malnutrition, recovered survival across generations via upregulated lysosome-rich enterocyte endocytic components enabling enhanced protein absorption, plus immune-gene transcriptional changes. Adaptation emerged gradually over generations and recurred in an independently generated allele under inbreeding.

papers.title: Altered regulation of septal peptidoglycan synthesis modulates β-lactam susceptibility in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
papers.summary: In Pseudomonas aeruginosa, substitutions in the FtsI pedestal domain bypass the need for FtsN and the FtsQLB complex in divisome activation. Some variants reduce β-lactam susceptibility while another causes FtsN-dependent hypersusceptibility, linking divisome regulation to β-lactam resistance in clinical isolates.

papers.title: Addressing the Blind Spots of Deaminase Base Editors with CRISPR-Cas Glycosylase-Based Editors.
papers.summary: Review of glycosylase-based CRISPR editors: DNA glycosylases, once sources of unwanted edits, now drive editors that achieve transversion mutations unreachable by deaminase base editors. The piece compares editor classes, covers repair-redirect mechanisms, therapy applications, and envisions AI-designed glycosylases for spatiotemporal genome control.

papers.title: PARP1 Constrains Insertional Prime Editing in a Context-Dependent Manner.
papers.summary: Screening 569 DNA-repair compounds found PARP inhibition boosts prime-editing insertions over 2-fold at HEK3 by removing PARP1's constraint. PARP1 loss phenocopied this across editor architectures and primary human T cells, though effects were locus- and RTT-dependent, without increasing indels.

papers.title: The adaptor protein ARAP contributes to Akt-dependent NF-κB p50 activation and inflammatory cytokine production in dendritic cells.
papers.summary: The adaptor protein ARAP is required for LPS-induced cytokine production in dendritic cells. ARAP knockout spared MAPK, IκBα degradation, and p65 translocation but impaired NF-κB p50 nuclear translocation via attenuated AKT phosphorylation, revealing a non-canonical, AKT-dependent route to p50 activation.

papers.title: ANKRD28 interacts with DOCK180 to activate Rac1-STAT3-Myc signaling and sustain stemness of CD34(+) leukemia stem cells in acute myeloid leukemia.
papers.summary: ANKRD28 is overexpressed in CD34+ leukemia stem cells in AML, correlating with relapse and poor prognosis. It binds DOCK180 to activate Rac1-STAT3-Myc signaling; knockdown suppresses stemness, prolongs survival in PDX models, and reduces infiltration, positioning ANKRD28 as an AML stemness dependency.

papers.title: Gallic acid partially attenuates thiomersal-associated oxidative, apoptotic, and CREB/BDNF-related alterations in rat hippocampal and prefrontal cortex tissues and systemic inflammatory responses.
papers.summary: In rats, thiomersal raised lipid peroxidation (MDA), TNF-α, and apoptotic markers while lowering BDNF. Gallic acid co-treatment partially reversed these oxidative, inflammatory, apoptotic, and CREB/BDNF-related changes, with significant interaction effects across tissue and serum markers during thiomersal exposure.

papers.title: Design, green synthesis, and anticancer evaluation of novel sulfaguanidine-based heterocycles as multi-target inhibitors of the VEGFR-2/PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway.
papers.summary: Novel sulfaguanidine-derived pyrimidine/triazine compounds were synthesized via microwave-assisted green chemistry and screened against five cancer lines. Leads 3 and 4 showed selective cytotoxicity (compound 4 IC50 4.87 µM in A431), downregulated VEGFR-2/PI3K/AKT/mTOR and CDC42, upregulated caspase-3, and arrested cells in G1 or G2/M.

papers.title: A Chemogenetic System for Spatiotemporal Perturbation of Cellular Methylation Potential.
papers.summary: A chemogenetic system uses plant methyltransferase EOMT1 to consume intracellular SAM upon eugenol addition, depleting SAM within 30 minutes at controlled levels. Differential sensitivities of H3K4me3, H3K9me3, and H3K27me3 marks revealed distinct histone methyltransferase/demethylase kinetics and organelle-level SAM coupling.

papers.title: Proteolytic Activation of T Cell Engagers And Bispecific Proteins Using Modular Coiled-Coil Peptides.
papers.summary: Protease-responsive masked T-cell engagers use coiled-coil zipper masking of anti-CD3 Fabs, reducing CD3 affinity ~400-800-fold until tumor protease cleavage. MMP2-cleavable constructs restored binding upon unmasking and enabled MMP2-dependent killing of PSMA+ and HER2+ cancer cells, addressing on-target off-tumor toxicity.

papers.title: Engineering a Ribozyme with Aminoacyl-tRNA Synthetase Activity.
papers.summary: A ribozyme was engineered by fusing a T-box riboswitch tRNA-binding module to flexizyme, creating an RNA with aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase-like activity. It aminoacylates target tRNAs, is redesignable for altered tRNA specificity, and supports in vitro translation recoding to site-specifically incorporate non-canonical amino acids.

papers.title: Time-Resolved Effects of Cold Atmospheric Plasma on E. coli GW-AmxH19 Transcriptome and Proteome in an Emulated Wastewater Environment.
papers.summary: Cold atmospheric plasma treatment of hospital-wastewater E. coli killed ~90% of cells. Survivors mounted short-term repair responses but transiently transcribed conjugative plasmid resistance genes; later recovery featured massive prophage activation, suggesting plasma's potential as a wastewater purification step with AMR-spread caveats.

papers.title: Parent-of-origin dependent allelic regulation of social behaviors in mice by noncanonically imprinted monoamine synthesis genes.
papers.summary: Th and Ddc show tissue-specific noncanonical imprinting in mice. In males, maternal Th null alleles reduce sociability while paternal Ddc null alleles increase aggression and impair social recognition, matching hypothalamic maternal-biased expression. First evidence that noncanonical imprinting shapes mammalian social behavior.

papers.title: Active and unusually expanded PIF/Harbinger transposable elements in the Caenorhabditis inopinata genome.
papers.summary: In C. inopinata, expanded PIF/Harbinger transposon families show functional partitioning: a single DDE transposase source supplies catalytic activity in trans while MADF-only copies expand. A second, older family (1,376 copies) lacks any DDE source and shows decay, illustrating bipartite transposon aging.

papers.title: Molas have mighty mitochondria: intensified purifying selection on mtDNA despite presumed "low-energy" lifestyles in ocean sunfishes (family Molidae).
papers.journal: Evolution; international journal of organic evolution
papers.summary: Contrary to the 'low-energy drifter' image, ocean sunfish show intensified purifying selection on mitochondrial genes (lower dN/dS across all mtDNA-encoded genes) consistent with active swimming, deep vertical migrations, and thermoregulation. Across 64 fish species, mtDNA rates didn't correlate with swimming speed.

papers.title: Riboflavin-sensitized UVA collagen crosslinking produced a controllable, dose-dependent increase in the nanomechanical strength of ex vivo bovine dura mater.
papers.summary: Riboflavin-sensitized UVA crosslinking of ex vivo bovine dura mater increased stiffness up to 150-fold (53 to ~8,000 kPa) in a strongly linear riboflavin dose-response (R² 0.994). Proof-of-concept for titratable biochemical dural reinforcement, potentially for neurosurgical dural repair.

papers.title: Dioscin attenuates D‑galactose‑induced retinal pigment epithelium senescence and epithelial-mesenchymal transition via the TGF‑β2/PI3K/Akt/β‑catenin pathway.
papers.summary: In D-galactose-induced senescence models, dioscin alleviated RPE senescence and EMT by suppressing the TGF-β2/PI3K/Akt/β-catenin pathway. Single-cell transcriptomics showed TGF-β2 upregulation in choroidal vascular endothelial cells in AMD patients, suggesting a paracrine vascular-RPE mechanism and potential AMD therapeutic angle.

papers.title: Development of mechanically optimized biomimetic hybrid scaffold-stem cell constructs for functional tendon regeneration and restoration of mechanical integrity.
papers.summary: A biomimetic hybrid scaffold combining tendon-derived stem cells, TGF-β3-loaded PLGA microspheres, and cyclic mechanical preconditioning restored 88% of native Achilles tendon tensile strength at 6 weeks and 95% at 12 weeks in rats, with aligned collagen, minimal adhesions, and reduced inflammation.

papers.title: Conformational insights into the unfolding pathway of RNA recognition motif (RRM) domain of TAF15 associated with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
papers.summary: Molecular dynamics simulations map the urea/temperature-induced unfolding of TAF15's RNA-recognition motif, an ALS-associated protein. β-sheets unfold preferentially, and heterogeneous partially unfolded intermediates persist, stabilized by rearranged native hydrogen bonds — conformers potentially relevant to aggregation in ALS pathology.

papers.title: Potential anti-inflammatory effect of L-carvone in endothelial dysfunction triggered by uremia related to chronic kidney disease.
papers.summary: L-carvone reduced IL-1β, IL-6, IL-8, VEGF-A, SAA, TNF-α, and MCP-1 in human endothelial cells exposed to uremic serum, plus reduced monocyte migration, without affecting viability. Suggests anti-inflammatory potential for uremia-driven endothelial dysfunction in chronic kidney disease.

papers.title: Selenium pretreatment alleviates ANIT-induced cholestasis by preserving BSEP expression and hepatic redox homeostasis.
papers.summary: In rats, selenium pre-treatment dose-dependently protected against ANIT-induced cholestatic liver injury, preserving BSEP/MRP2/NTCP bile-acid transporters, rebalancing bile-acid homeostasis, activating NRF2/HO-1 and SIRT1, and suppressing TLR4/NF-κB inflammation, with the 1 mg/kg dose showing significant benefit across most parameters.

papers.title: Genomic characterization of CTX-M-15-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae ST709-KL9 from neonatal bacteraemia in eastern India.
papers.summary: First report of CTX-M-15-producing, multidrug-resistant K. pneumoniae ST709-KL9 from neonatal bacteremia in eastern India. Genome analysis found multiple resistance genes and point mutations; the isolate remained susceptible to meropenem, amikacin, and colistin, underscoring the need for genomic AMR surveillance.

papers.title: Association of miR-199a-3p and CDK7 expression with clinicopathological features of breast cancer.
papers.summary: In 30 breast cancer patients, miR-199a-3p was significantly downregulated in tumor tissue (0.506-fold, p=0.0029) with moderate diagnostic power (AUC 0.720); a combined miR-199a-3p/CDK7 model reached AUC 0.750 with 76.7% sensitivity and 80% specificity. CDK7 associated with PR-negative status.

papers.title: Phytochemicals modulating TGF-β signaling in radiation-induced fibrosis.
papers.summary: Review of phytochemicals (curcumin, resveratrol, EGCG, quercetin, berberine, honokiol, silibinin) modulating TGF-β signaling in radiation-induced fibrosis. Preclinical data show reduced fibrosis markers, but most evidence comes from non-radiation fibrosis models; clinical signals exist for dermatitis/mucositis but require larger trials.

papers.title: CD47-mediated efferocytosis in diseases: A comprehensive review.
papers.summary: Review of CD47-SIRPα 'don't eat me' signaling in efferocytosis: pathological CD47 upregulation lets abnormal cells evade clearance, promoting tumors, atherosclerosis, autoimmunity, and neurodegeneration. Summarizes mechanisms and therapeutic potential of targeting the CD47/SIRPα immune checkpoint across diseases.

papers.title: Combination of kale-derived exosomes and dactolisib promotes apoptosis and modulates iron homeostasis in Hep3B hepatocellular carcinoma cells.
papers.summary: Kale-derived exosome-like nanovesicles alone didn't affect Hep3B viability, but combined with the PI3K/mTOR inhibitor dactolisib they reduced viability, downregulated AKT/mTOR/MDM2, increased TP53/caspase-3, and modulated ROS and iron homeostasis — inducing apoptosis rather than ferroptosis in this HCC cell line.

papers.title: Shikonin attenuates doxorubicin-induced myocardial senescence and fibrosis in association with improved redox and mitochondrial homeostasis.
papers.summary: Shikonin protected rats from doxorubicin cardiotoxicity, improving cardiac function, redox status, and mitochondrial homeostasis while reducing senescence markers (p53/p21) and fibrosis. DRP1 knockdown in H9c2 cells mimicked protection, implicating mitochondrial fission regulation in shikonin's cardioprotective mechanism.

papers.title: Cannabidiol (CBD) differentially shapes systemic cytokines and transcriptomic profiles in the liver and spleen: insights from a male mouse model.
papers.summary: In male mice, CBD reduced IL-1β and TNF-α acutely and IL-6 during longer exposure, with liver showing strong dose- and time-dependent transcriptomic remodeling (mitochondrial, lipid metabolism, circadian pathways) while spleen changes were modest — highlighting organ- and regimen-specific immunomodulatory effects.

papers.title: Hereditary breast cancer: emerging roles of non-coding RNAs.
papers.summary: Review of non-coding RNAs in hereditary breast cancer: covers genetic susceptibility loci, ncRNA roles in tumor progression and therapeutic resistance, plus emerging strategies including immunotherapy, precision medicine, and nanoparticle delivery. Emphasizes integrative, personalized approaches given heterogeneity and access challenges.
